samples.text:
The diagram shows how a solar water heating system give hot water to a house. There are six stages and it is a cycle.

First, there is a solar panel on the roof of the house. The sunlight heats the fluid which is in the dark pipes of the panel. Then the hot fluid rises and it is carried to the storage cylinder.

In the storage cylinder there is a heat exchanger. It is a coil and it transfer the heat from the fluid to the water of the house. After that, the hot water is kept in a insulated cylinder, so the people in the house can use it later.

On cloudy days, there is not so much sun, so a backup boiler heats the water. Finally, the fluid which is cooled is returned to the solar panel by a pump, and then the cycle start again.

Overall, the system uses the sun to heat the water, but when the weather is cloudy it needs the boiler too. The fluid goes round and round between the panel and the cylinder, so it is used many times.
samples.why: Overview given late but relevant · all six stages covered and the cycle noted · simple linking · repetitive vocabulary · agreement, article and word choice errors that do not obscure meaning.

samples.text:
The diagram illustrates how a solar water heating system supplies a house with hot water.

Overall, the system works in a cycle of six stages, in which a fluid is heated by the sun, gives its heat to the household water and then returns to the solar panel to be heated again. A backup boiler is also included for cloudy days.

The process begins at the solar panel on the roof, where sunlight heats a fluid inside dark pipes. As it becomes hot, this fluid rises and is carried to the storage cylinder. Inside the cylinder, a coil known as a heat exchanger transfer the heat from the fluid to the household water, which is then kept in an insulated cylinder until it is needed.

On cloudy days, a backup boiler is used to heat the water, which means the house still has hot water when there is less sunshine. Meanwhile, the fluid which has cooled down is returned to the panel by a pump, and the cycle is repeated as the fluid is heated by the sun once more.
samples.why: Clear overview explaining the loop and backup · logical progression with passives and relative clauses · appropriate vocabulary (heat exchanger, insulated) · frequent error-free sentences with one agreement slip.

samples.text:
The diagram explains how a solar water heating system provides a house with hot water, using sunlight as its primary source of energy.

The system operates as a continuous six-stage loop in which a fluid circulates between a roof-mounted solar panel and a storage cylinder, collecting heat at one end and releasing it at the other, before being pumped back to begin again. A backup boiler supplements the system when the weather is cloudy.

The cycle begins on the roof, where sunlight heats a fluid flowing through the dark pipes of the solar panel. Once heated, the fluid rises and is carried to the storage cylinder, where a coil acting as a heat exchanger transfers its heat to the household water. This water is then retained in an insulated cylinder so that it stays hot until required.

On overcast days, a backup boiler is used to heat the water. Having given up its heat, the cooled fluid is pumped back up to the panel on the roof, where it is warmed once again by the sun, allowing the process to repeat without interruption.
samples.why: Skilful overview describing the loop and supplementary boiler · stages sequenced fluently · precise vocabulary (circulates, supplements, overcast) · wide range of participle and passive structures · error-free.
